summary: Cross-tenant DoS via uninitialized LogprobsTensors with prompt_logprobs

### Summary

`LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu()` in `vllm/v1/outputs.py` allocates the backing int32 tensor with `torch.empty()`, leaving it uninitialized.  When the V1 model runner fills logprobs for a request whose prefix is reported as externally computed by a `KVConnectorBase_V1` subclass, positions `[0 .. num_computed_tokens - 1]` are never written.  Downstream `tokenizer.decode()` on those positions hits garbage int32 values and raises `OverflowError`.  The exception propagates out of `EngineCore`, the engine process dies, and every in-flight request on that engine — including co-tenant traffic — is lost.

A single API request with `prompt_logprobs` (or `logprobs` + `echo=true`) against a connector-cached prefix is sufficient to trigger the crash.  The trigger is cross-tenant: an attacker only needs to share an `EngineCore` with the victim.

### Details

**Affected configuration**

- V1 engine
- Any `KVConnectorBase_V1` subclass whose `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` returns `num_new > 0`
- A client request with `sampling_params.prompt_logprobs is not None` (or `echo=true` + `logprobs` over the OpenAI-compatible API)

In-tree connectors that meet this condition:

- `LMCacheConnectorV1` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/lmcache_connector.py`) — fires on any prefix cache hit.
- `NixlConnector` (`.../nixl_connector.py`) — fires on the decode side of disaggregated P/D (`do_remote_prefill=True`).
- `SharedStorageConnector`, `P2pNcclConnector`, `OffloadingConnector`, `MultiConnector` — same shape.
- Any out-of-tree `KVConnectorBase_V1` subclass.

The local prefix cache is **not** affected: `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:169-172` returns `(empty, 0)` from `get_computed_blocks()` whenever `sampling_params.prompt_logprobs is not None`.  No KV connector replicates that gate.


**Regression history**

This is a regression, not a long-standing bug.  The original V1 prompt-logprobs path computed each chunk fresh and assigned the result directly, so every position in `LogprobsTensors` was a real computed value by construction.

- **Regression introduced:** [PR #14875](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/14875), commit `3aee6573dc58cf758054947039a498353c895d6a` (*[V1] Aggregate chunked prompt logprobs in model runner*, 2025-03-24).  Added `LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu()` using `torch.empty()` and switched to a pre-allocate-then-slice-fill pattern with `chunk_slice = slice(start_idx, start_idx + num_logits)`, `start_idx = request.num_computed_tokens`.  Correct in isolation: production code paths at merge time always had `num_computed_tokens=0` on the first scheduling step, so the first chunk wrote from position 0 and subsequent chunks tiled forward.  The new invariant the rewrite introduced — *"the destination buffer may have unwritten positions"* — was never reconciled with anything else, because nothing else made it reachable yet.

- **Reachable:** [PR #15960](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/15960), commit `3408e4715` (*[P/D][V1] KV Connector API V1*, 2025-04-17).  24 days later.  `connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens()` lets an external system report tokens as already computed, so a request can now enter the model runner with `num_computed_tokens > 0` on the very first scheduling step.  Positions `[0 .. num_computed_tokens - 1]` are now permanently unwritten.

- **First user-visible exposure:** [PR #16625](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/16625), commit `5e83a7277` (*[v1] [P/D] Adding LMCache KV connector for v1*, 2025-04-25).  First in-tree connector that returns `num_new > 0` on prefix hits in normal serving, not just disaggregated prefill.

- **Worse failure mode:** [PR #17751](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/17751), commit `d19110204` (*[P/D] NIXL Integration*, 2025-05-12).  Disagg path can mark the entire prompt as externally computed, producing the fully-uninitialized-tensor variant on the decode side.

### Impact

- Remote-trigger crash of `EngineCore` on a single malformed request.
- **Scope change:** the crash kills *every* in-flight request on the engine, not just the offender's.  Co-tenant traffic and in-progress batches are dropped.
- Trivial to trigger: warm a prefix (or rely on natural cache reuse), then send a request with `prompt_logprobs` set.  Repeatable as a kill-loop.
- Highest real-world exposure: `lm-eval-harness` multiple-choice workloads (MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, BBH, PIQA) against vLLM + LMCache.  MC tasks require `prompt_logprobs` by definition and share per-subject prefixes by construction; item 2 of any subject is a guaranteed crash on a connector-equipped server.

### Patches

Replace `torch.empty()` with `torch.zeros()` for token IDs and `torch.full(-inf)` for logprobs in `LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu()`.  Zero is a valid token ID that decodes safely; `-inf` is the correct "not computed" sentinel and matches the existing convention for out-of-top-k positions.  All non-connector code paths overwrite every position, so the initial values are dead writes in the common case — no behavior change for any previously-working code path.

~~~diff
diff --git a/vllm/v1/outputs.py b/vllm/v1/outputs.py
index e6cc6019b..be34ece7d 100644
--- a/vllm/v1/outputs.py
+++ b/vllm/v1/outputs.py
@@ -48,14 +48,21 @@ class LogprobsTensors(NamedTuple):
     @staticmethod
     def empty_cpu(num_positions: int,
                   num_tokens_per_position: int) -> "LogprobsTensors":
-        """Create empty LogprobsTensors on CPU."""
+        """Create zero-initialized LogprobsTensors on CPU.

-        logprob_token_ids = torch.empty(
+        Uses zeros instead of uninitialized memory so that positions
+        that are never filled (e.g. externally-computed KV connector
+        tokens) have valid token IDs and sentinel logprobs rather than
+        garbage values that crash the tokenizer.
+        """
+
+        logprob_token_ids = torch.zeros(
             (num_positions, num_tokens_per_position),
             dtype=torch.int32,
             device="cpu")
-        logprobs = torch.empty_like(logprob_token_ids, dtype=torch.float32)
-        selected_token_ranks = torch.empty(num_positions,
+        logprobs = torch.full_like(logprob_token_ids, float("-inf"),
+                                   dtype=torch.float32)
+        selected_token_ranks = torch.zeros(num_positions,
                                            dtype=torch.int32,
                                            device="cpu")
         return LogprobsTensors(
~~~

The upstream commit should carry a `Fixes:` trailer pointing at the regression commit, to let maintainers triage backports automatically:

~~~
Fixes: 3aee6573dc58 ("[V1] Aggregate chunked prompt logprobs in model runner")
~~~

### Workarounds

Until the patch is deployed, any one of the following mitigates the issue:

- **Disable KV connectors** on the affected engine (drop `--kv-transfer-config` and any `kv_transfer_config` setting).  Local prefix caching is unaffected and remains available.
- **Strip `prompt_logprobs`, `logprobs`, and `echo` from inbound requests** at an API gateway or middleware in front of vLLM.  These are the only request-level switches that reach the crash path.
- **Apply the one-line patch above** (`torch.empty` → `torch.zeros` / `torch.full(-inf)` in `vllm/v1/outputs.py`).  No new dependencies, no behavior change on any non-connector path.

### Affected versions

**Latent (regression present, not reachable in the field).**  Bug code sits in `LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu()` but no caller can drive `num_computed_tokens > 0` into the slice-fill path.  No user-visible failure mode in normal use.

- `v0.8.2`, `v0.8.3`, `v0.8.4` — first releases to ship the regression commit `3aee6573d` (PR #14875, merged 2025-03-24), but predate the V1 KV Connector API.

These become reachable only if a V1 KV connector is backported into them, which is unlikely but worth flagging for downstream distributors who maintain their own branches.

**Reachable and user-visible.**  Both the regression and a connector path that can drive `num_computed_tokens > 0` on the first scheduling step are present.

- `v0.8.5`, `v0.8.5.post1` — first tagged versions containing the regression, the V1 KV Connector API (`3408e4715`, PR #15960), and `LMCacheConnectorV1` (`5e83a7277`, PR #16625).  First release where an LMCache + `prompt_logprobs` user can crash the engine with a single request.
- `v0.9.0` onward — adds NIXL (`d19110204`, PR #17751, 2025-05-12).  Introduces the full-prompt-uninitialized variant on the decode side of disaggregated P/D.
- Every subsequent release through HEAD: `v0.9.0.1`, `v0.9.1`, `v0.9.2`, `v0.10.0`, `v0.10.1`, `v0.10.1.1`, `v0.10.2`, `v0.11.0`, `v0.11.1`, `v0.18.0`, `v0.18.1`, `v0.19.0`, and all intermediate release candidates (`v0.10.0rc1` through `v0.19.1rc0`).  The fix has not landed upstream; current `main` is still affected.

**Not affected.**

- `≤ v0.8.1` — pre-regression.  `prompt_logprobs_dict[req_id]` was assigned fresh tensors computed each chunk; no uninitialized memory existed on this path.

**Backport target.**  Affects `v0.8.5` and later — every release containing both the chunked-logprobs aggregation rewrite from PR #14875 and the V1 KV Connector API from PR #15960.  Minimum backport target: the latest maintained minor release.  Ideal coverage: also `v0.10.x` and `v0.11.x` if those are still seeing point releases, since the LMCache + `lm-eval` user population on those branches is the largest exposed cohort.

### Residual gap (separate follow-up, not part of this advisory)

After this patch, `echo=true` over a connector-cached region returns `(token_id=0, logprob=-inf)` for the cached span instead of the "true" logprobs of the prompt.  This is a strict improvement over the previous behavior (engine crash) and the sentinel is unambiguous, but it is a correctness gap for callers that genuinely want prompt-logprobs over cached prefixes.

The principled follow-up is to mirror the local-APC gate inside the connector dispatch path: skip external matching when `sampling_params.prompt_logprobs is not None`.  This matches the existing behavior of `kv_cache_manager.py:169-172` and is the smallest change that restores correctness.  Happy to write that patch separately once this floor lands.

### Coordination request

The downstream blast radius is broader than vLLM itself.  Requesting the vLLM VMT coordinate prenotification with the following projects before public release:

- **LMCache** (`github.com/LMCache/LMCache`, `SECURITY.md`, `contact@lmcache.ai`) — highest user exposure; the prefix-reuse workload LMCache markets is the exact trigger condition.
- **NIXL / NVIDIA Dynamo** (`github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo`) — narrower request volume but 100% trigger rate when a logprobs request hits a P/D decode node.
- **llm-d**, **vLLM Production Stack**, **KServe** — ship vLLM with LMCache integration.
